clinicalPearls: A rare adult form of cutaneous mastocytosis characterised by persistent telangiectatic red-brown macules
Lesions are typically on the trunk and may be widespread, with fine telangiectasia within them
The Darier sign is often subtle or absent, unlike in typical urticaria pigmentosa
It occurs almost exclusively in adults and may be associated with systemic mastocytosis
Diagnosis relies on biopsy demonstrating increased mast cells around dilated dermal vessels
Evaluation for systemic disease and mediator symptoms is appropriate given the adult onset
reference.pathophysiology: Telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans is a variant of cutaneous mastocytosis in which increased dermal mast cells cluster around dilated superficial blood vessels, producing persistent telangiectatic pigmented macules. As in other mastocytosis, clonal mast cells (often KIT-associated) release mediators, though the weal-and-flare response is frequently muted. Because it presents in adults, it is regarded, like other adult cutaneous mastocytosis, as potentially reflecting underlying systemic mast cell disease.
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy with mast cell staining around dermal vessels
Assessment for systemic mastocytosis in view of adult onset
History of mediator symptoms and triggers
reference.prognosis: The cutaneous lesions are persistent but benign; prognosis is influenced by any associated systemic mastocytosis, which should be sought given the adult onset.
pitfalls: Expecting a florid Darier sign, which is often absent
Confusing it with non-mast-cell telangiectatic disorders
Not measuring tryptase in an adult with suggestive lesions
